subject.title: fix(agents): normalize bare date filenames to memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md in…

question: Should OpenClaw accept this ENOENT-only bare-date fallback in the generic read wrapper, including its explicit second-path workspace validation, despite the linked report being closed as not planned?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent and proven, but repository policy treats fallback behavior and filesystem confinement as intentional product and security-boundary choices that automation cannot authorize.

options.title: Accept Guarded Fallback
options.body: Rebase the branch, confirm the synthesized-path guard remains equivalent to current workspace confinement, and land the narrowly scoped fallback.

options.title: Repair Earlier Path Preservation
options.body: Reject generic filename inference and instead preserve or reinforce the `memory/` prefix before the model-generated read reaches the tool wrapper.

options.title: Keep Not-Planned Direction
options.body: Close this PR consistently with the linked issue if maintainers do not want OpenClaw to compensate for model-generated bare daily-memory paths.

recommendation.title: Accept Guarded Fallback
recommendation.body: Rebase the branch, confirm the synthesized-path guard remains equivalent to current workspace confinement, and land the narrowly scoped fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history in the read-wrapper workspace-root boundary makes this the closest available routing candidate for the fallback and confinement decision.
